cards.text: This is a letter from Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the elect who are exiles scattered across Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia. Exiles, friend. Folks living far from home, and trust me, a stamper who spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer knows that feeling.

cards.question: Peter says these exiles were chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father. Who does he say sanctified them?

cards.text: Chosen by the Father, sanctified by the Spirit, for obedience to Jesus Christ and sprinkling by His blood. And after ALL that, Peter finally gets around to hello: "Grace and peace be yours in abundance."

cards.question: Peter bursts into praise: "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ!" He says that by His great mercy, God has given them new birth. Into what?
Peter says that living hope comes through the ___ of Jesus Christ from the dead.

cards.text: That same new birth is also into an inheritance. And friend, this is NOT the kind where your uncle leaves you a dusty recliner and a shoebox of old receipts.

cards.question: True or false: Peter says this inheritance will slowly fade over time.
Peter says this inheritance is reserved in ___ for them.
While they wait, Peter says these believers are shielded through faith by God's ___ for the salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.

cards.text: In all this they greatly rejoice. But Peter keeps it real: for a little while, they may have had to suffer grief in various trials.

Those trials prove the character of their faith, and Peter holds it up next to gold refined by fire. Faith that's been through the heat, friend, and I'll tell you, the heat is where the good stuff happens.

cards.question: Peter says their proven faith is more precious than gold. True or false: he says gold perishes, even though it's refined by fire.
Peter says that proven faith will result in praise, glory and honor. When?

answers.text: At the revelation of Jesus Christ
When Peter comes to visit them

cards.question: Peter's readers have never seen Jesus. True or false: Peter says they love Him and believe in Him anyway.
Peter says they rejoice with an inexpressible and glorious ___ as they receive the goal of their faith, the salvation of their ___.

cards.text: Then Peter looks back. The prophets who foretold this grace searched and investigated carefully, trying to figure out the time and setting the Spirit of Christ in them was pointing to.

cards.question: Peter says the Spirit of Christ in those prophets predicted two things about Christ. What were they?

answers.text: His sufferings and the glories to follow
His birth and His baptism in the river
His kingdom and the temple He would build

cards.text: And here's the twist. It was revealed to those prophets that all that work wasn't for themselves, and friend, I KNOW that one: you bake all day, and the cookies go to somebody else's party.

cards.question: The prophets weren't serving themselves. Who does Peter say they were serving?
What the prophets foretold is now announced by those who preached the gospel by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven. True or false: Peter says even angels long to look into these things.

findings.problem: "Chosen by the Father" changes what the text says. 1 Peter 1:1-2 says they were "chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father." The text doesn't say the Father did the choosing. Card 2 words it correctly, so card 3 now says something different from card 2.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "A promised land" is too close to something true in the passage. In 1:4, the same new birth is also into an inheritance, and in Scripture the land is the classic inheritance. A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The setup joke gives away card 7. It says this inheritance is NOT like a "dusty recliner and a shoebox of old receipts," which rules out an inheritance that fades over time. Card 7 then asks whether it fades.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "The heat is where the good stuff happens" sounds like a nice dad being pleasant, not a laugh-out-loud line. The oven and heat idea is a good chance for a real joke.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The right answer, "At the revelation of Jesus Christ," sounds like the Bible. The wrong answers, "When Peter comes to visit them" and "When they return to Jerusalem," sound plain and everyday. The right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The second blank, "the salvation of their ___," can't be reasoned out. "Families" makes just as much sense as "souls." The only way to pick is to already know the wording.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question says "they rejoice" but never says who "they" are. It leans on card 14, which is no longer on screen. It should name Peter's readers.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
